newsitem.title: FRANCE: France says EU should end wheat tax, resume exports.
newsitem.headline: France says EU should end wheat tax, resume exports.

text.p: France's cereals authority, accusing Brussels of putting Europe's image as a food supplier at risk, urged the European Union on Wednesday to drop a controversial wheat export tax and resume suspended exports.

Alain Moulinier, director general of the semi-public ONIC grain authority, said the tax of five Ecus ($6) per tonne designed to prevent exports was "not justified" and was preventing European farmers from competing on world markets.

"France's position is clear. It is that the level of tax...is unjustified and that we must get ready to export as soon as possible in the new campaign," Moulinier told a news conference, referring to exports from this year's harvest, which is now around one month away.
The European Commission overrode French opposition a month ago to impose a wheat tax for the second time in a year to save supplies for domestic consumers and prevent local prices rising.

But traders have for weeks been pressing the EU executive to restore a system of export subsidies and allow them to start selling before the harvest arrives, while U.S. opposition to the European tax will be on the agenda for farm talks on June 16.

Moulinier said that rather than blocking exports with a tax, Brussels should be awarding subsidies of 12 Ecus ($14) a tonne. And he raised concerns that Europe would damage its trade image by holding back wheat. "One may fear that using the tax harms the (EU) Community's image with foreign buyers," he said.
